findings.aws_behavior: Without partial-batch reporting, one failed record returns every message in the batch to the queue.
findings.impact: Already-completed side effects can repeat and poison messages can block healthy work.
findings.remediation: Enable ReportBatchItemFailures and return only failed messageId values; keep side effects idempotent.
findings.title: SQS consumer replays the entire failed batch
findings.verification: Inject one poison and one healthy message and confirm only the poison message is retried.

findings.aws_behavior: A poison message can be retried until retention expiry and repeatedly consume concurrency.
findings.evidence: RedrivePolicy is absent on a Lambda event-source queue.
findings.impact: Bad input can stall or inflate the cost of healthy processing without a quarantine path.
findings.remediation: Attach a DLQ with a bounded maxReceiveCount and define a reviewed replay procedure.
findings.title: Consumed SQS queue has no redrive policy
findings.verification: In AWS, inject a poison message and verify bounded receipt count, DLQ arrival, and alarm state.

findings.aws_behavior: AWS recommends at least six times the function timeout plus the batch window for Lambda SQS sources.
findings.evidence: VisibilityTimeout=30; required baseline is at least 120 seconds for this consumer.
findings.impact: A message can become visible during processing, producing concurrent duplicates.
findings.remediation: Increase visibility timeout or reduce the function timeout, then retain idempotent effects.
findings.title: SQS visibility timeout is shorter than the Lambda retry window
findings.verification: Measure processing duration and duplicate receipt behavior with a slow-message AWS canary.

findings.aws_behavior: Lambda may scale until account or downstream limits are reached.
findings.impact: A traffic spike can amplify DynamoDB, S3, Step Functions, and logging cost or throttle sibling workloads.
findings.remediation: Set and load-test a workload-specific concurrency cap; monitor throttles and age-of-oldest-message.
findings.title: Lambda concurrency is unbounded at the function level
findings.verification: Run a bounded load test in AWS and inspect concurrency, throttles, backlog age, and downstream capacity.

findings.aws_behavior: Cross-service request correlation requires runtime trace evidence in AWS.
findings.evidence: Tracing is not Active in Globals or the function.
findings.impact: Diagnosing retries, duplication, and latency becomes slower.
findings.remediation: Enable active tracing and log only identifiers and low-cardinality fields, never templates or upload URLs.
findings.title: Lambda tracing is disabled
findings.verification: Run the AWS canary and confirm traces connect API, Lambda, and downstream SDK calls.
